Public-domain example: Pride and Prejudice

Generated with Lixity 0.7.1. The dashboard shows the first 3 chapters of Pride and Prejudice (Jane Austen); the complete work is available as a PDF analysis report.

The opening chapters are reproduced from a public-domain Project Gutenberg edition. The report uses the real chapter, paragraph and style interactions of the renderer, without server functions; it accepts no uploads and saves no edits.

Short excerpts and language-dependent heuristics support human review. This example is not a benchmark, a calibration corpus or a literary quality verdict.

Scenes & style registers

Each scene is measured separately. Registers and target ranges are project choices, not quality judgments. Chapters serve as scenes when no dividers are present. Set assignments and targets in lixity.toml.

Word and sentence counts show the sample size. HD-D is unavailable below 100 words; sentence variation needs at least two sentences. Standard errors are approximations, not validated confidence intervals. A dash means unavailable; even an observed zero does not establish certainty.

Method, coverage and exact loadings

PCA combines standardized low-to-high feature ranks within the complete chapters. The origin is their mean rank position; scores are component coordinates, not z scores.

Axes depend on this manuscript and its measured chapters. Similarity is limited to these features and displayed dimensions. Variation does not measure literary importance or quality; a cutoff does not prescribe an edit.
